small_guidance:
- The conv (128×8→64, 3×3, 128×128) likely dominates runtime; tuning the GN/LSE tail further yields little. But within the current structure, try fusing the stats kernel and the apply-LSE into a single persistent kernel per `(N, group)` that computes mean/var, then loops channels-in-group to apply norm+tanh+hardswish+residual and accumulates LSE — eliminating one full read of `x_conv`.
- Add autotune configs to `gn_stats_kernel` (BLOCK_HW 512/1024/2048, num_warps 4/8) instead of fixed 1024/8; HW=15876 so BLOCK_HW=2048 with num_warps=8 may halve loop iterations.
- For `fused_apply_lse_kernel`, add larger BLOCK_HW (2048, 4096) configs and try num_stages=3; the inner loop is `static_range(64)` so register pressure is high — also try num_warps=4 with BLOCK_HW=512 to relieve it.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)` with BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=128 (HW), BLOCK_K=ICxKHxKW=72. Conv is the heaviest op (128×64×126×126×8×9 ≈ 7.5 GFLOPs/batch element) and is the largest remaining headroom.
- Fuse conv → GN stats → norm+tanh+hardswish+residual → LSE into a two-stage pipeline: stage 1 = conv kernel that writes `x_conv` and per-(N,group) partial sums via atomics or a separate reduction; stage 2 = single fused kernel doing normalization, activation, residual, and online LSE in one sweep over channels per spatial tile.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) layout end-to-end so the channel axis is contiguous: this makes the GN per-spatial-pixel reduction across channels coalesced and lets the LSE channel-loop be a contiguous load rather than strided by HW.
